stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: All provisionally selected Haj pilgrims from Karnataka will have to undergo a mandatory two-stage medical screening and fitness certification process before proceeding for Haj 2027, according to the Health Department..The Primary Medical Screening, which constitutes Stage I, will be conducted by allopathic medical officers at taluk and district hospitals, including government medical college hospitals..The screening will include prescribed diagnostic investigations..In Bengaluru, the facility will also be available at Victoria Hospital, Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, K C General Hospital, Jayanagar General Hospital and Sri C V Raman General Hospital..CIC faults central Haj Committee for denying info under RTI on Mumbai's Haj House expenditure, contract.Pilgrims have been asked to obtain the fitness certificate in the prescribed format and upload it, along with the payment slip or online payment receipt, on the Haj Committee of India (HCoI) portal..Physical copies must also be submitted to the office of the State Haj Committee in Bengaluru by September 15..The department has advised pilgrims to preserve the original fitness certificate and all investigation reports, as these will be required during Stage II medical screening and vaccination closer to the date of embarkation.

stories.headline: 'Fed up': The story behind Russia No. 1 Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoos
stories.deck: Russia’s No. 1 chess grandmaster Ian Nepomniachtchi has two tattoos. Both carry different stories. His left-arm full sleeve took eight sessions over eight months, with flights from Moscow to Munich to meet his tattoo artist. From a phoenix and a favourite quote to Greek mythology, chess pieces and the pain involved, Nepo opens up about the stories behind his ink.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The word “tattoo” is believed to have come from Polynesian languages, particularly words such as "tatau", a term associated with traditional body art in that region. European sailors encountered Polynesian tattooing and helped carry the word back into European languages. Even thousands of years earlier, ancient Egyptians were already tattooing their bodies, with some of the earliest known examples found on female mummies. Researchers suggest that their markings may have served social, ritual or protective purposes.
Millennia later, tattoos still carry stories. On the arms of Russia’s top-ranked chess grandmaster Ian Nepomniachtchi, they surely do.
A two-time back-to-back winner of the prestigious Candidates Tournament, Nepomniachtchi, affectionately known in the chess world simply as "Nepo", was initially slated to fly from Moscow to Bengaluru on September 2 for the Global Chess League (GCL).
Opting to delay his travel, he touched down on the morning of September 4, a day before the start of the tournament. The late arrival has effectively cost him any chance for local sightseeing, but the city has still managed to win him over.
"I really like the climate; it's very mild compared to what I'm used to in India when I visited previously. And yeah, the place is very nice," Nepo told TimesofIndia.com with a smile during an exclusive interaction as his team, Ganges Grandmasters, opened their GCL campaign with a victory on Saturday.
Whether you were inside the arena or watching from a screen, Nepomniachtchi’s arms were hard to miss. At a glance, they looked less like a grandmaster’s limbs and more like a vivid canvas, covered in colours and intricate artwork that stood out against the otherwise restrained setting of professional chess.
The elite circuit is a world of pristine blazers, pressed shirts and strict sartorial codes, where body art is rarely part of the picture. Here, at GCL, that is not the case.
"Normally, it's not approved by the dress code. So, this is only for a gym," Nepo admitted, laughing as he rolled back his sleeves to reveal his tattoo.
Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoo on his right arm (Photos by Jyotirmoy Halder from TimesofIndia
When asked how many he has. "Not that much, only two," he replied. On his right arm carries a powerful mantra. “Rise and rise again and again like the Phoenix from the ashes; until the lambs have become lions.”
"I have this one, but this comes from 2023. I think I played the first GCL right after getting this," he explained. "I like this quote. This I wanted to get many, many years before. It's always hard to make a decision to get something onto your skin."
The process for his right arm was surprisingly painless, which gave the grandmaster a false sense of security.
"This one felt so easy," Nepo recalled. "So, I felt, alright, maybe the full-sleeve is fine. Why not?"
A test of patience off the board
That casual "why not" evolved into an agonising, transatlantic project on his left arm that would test his endurance on another level.
"My nickname is Lachesis, and it's the Greek goddess of fate," he told this website, referencing his popular social media handle, lachesisq. "I wanted a Greek goddess, and it took me some time to find a master, an artist who specialises (in this)."
Nepo eventually found the right artist, but that artist was in Germany.
"The artist I was working with is based in Munich," he revealed. "It was logistically a bit tricky as I live in Moscow. We completed several sessions, and eventually, it was eight sessions total starting from September and ending in April."
Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoo on his left arm (Photos by Jyotirmoy Halder from TimesofIndia
The resulting full-sleeve is what one can call a chef-d'œuvre. "Eventually, it's a mix of ideas," the Russian grandmaster stated while examining the ink. "You have some snake for Ouroboros and also some chess pieces for whatever reason, but it was an idea from my artist, and I didn't really argue."
But for the 36-year-old Nepo, it was a classic case of no pain, no gain.
"This one (right arm) was completely painless, and this (left arm) was a hell of a time," he confessed. "I finished it (the left one) this year, but it's a full sleeve. It was quite painful, to be honest, and it took a while. 
So, for now, I'm fed up with pain. I was patient; I tolerated a lot."
Now that the suffering has ended with its completion, he doesn't plan on returning to the tattoo chair anytime soon. Now, he just hopes that people can see, and understand, the meaning behind the artwork.
"And this is supposed to be a phoenix," he said with a final grin, gesturing to his right arm, "if it's recognisable or not."

stories.headline: Cauvery row: Karnataka seeks sharp cut in quantum of water release to Tamil Nadu
stories.deck: K'taka seeks sharp cut in quantum of water release to TN
stories.bodyText: NEW DELHI: Karnataka has appealed to the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to reduce daily water releases to Tamil Nadu ordered by it, from 9,000 cusec to 2,000 cusec, at the Biligundlu inter-state border, citing critically low inflows to its Cauvery basin reservoirs..The CWMA had, on August 25, directed Karnataka to maintain a release of 9,000 cusec from that date till September 8, endorsing a Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) decision of August 24..A CWRC meeting is set for September 8, followed by a CWMA review of rainfall and crop conditions..In an appeal, water resources department additional chief secretary Gaurav Gupta said storage in Karnataka’s four major reservoirs stood at just 66.629 tmcft..Cauvery panel directs Karnataka to release 9,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.Likely inflows are not expected to exceed 20 tmcft amid an unprecedented super El Niño. The state would face shortages even without further releases to TN, he said..Karnataka has started releasing water for irrigation in the month of August. So far, about 15.124 tmcft (as on September 4), has flowed from the four reservoirs for supplementing irrigation in reduced areas of the Cauvery basin..Continued canal releases are essential to protect standing crops. The state’s remaining needs for irrigation, drinking water (including Bengaluru) and environmental flows total about 154 tmcft..Karnataka noted that Tamil Nadu’s Mettur reservoir holds about 55 tmcft, with expected intermediate catchment contributions of 45 tmcft or more, plus 6 tmcft in other reservoirs, providing roughly 100 tmcft..For the Samba crop sown over a reduced area, Tamil Nadu’s requirement from Mettur should not exceed about 95 tmcft, allowing it to manage without further releases from Karnataka, the state said in its appeal..It took objections to the hurried decisions by the CWRC and CWMA in July and August, instead of waiting till the end of the south west monsoon for a proper distress assessment, calling such ad hoc measures arbitrary and contrary to Karnataka’s equitable interests.

stories.headline: Two dead, two critical after small plane crashes in California
stories.bodyText:
Two people were killed and two others critically injured after a small plane crashed near Sierra Sky Park Airport in Fresno, California, in the US, on Saturday.
The aircraft crashed near Blythe Avenue, close to Sierra Sky Park Airport, according to ABC30 News, which cited the Fresno fire department. The circumstances leading to the crash were not immediately clear.
The two injured were taken to hospital in critical condition, the department said.
Several agencies responded to the crash site, including the Fresno police department, Fresno fire department, Fresno County sheriff’s office and North Central fire department, ABC30 News reported. Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) also responded after the incident affected power supplies in the surrounding area.
According to PG&E’s outage map, electricity was briefly disrupted for nearby residents following the crash. The outage was later restored. The US authorities have not yet released further details about the identities of those involved or what caused the aircraft to crash. The incident remains under investigation.

stories.headline: Indian-origin fraudster arrested, says FBI Director Kash Patel
stories.deck: Manjit Singh Bedi, who allegedly defrauded the U.S. government of $6 lakh, had a bounty of $1.5 lakh on his head
stories.bodyText:
A most-wanted fraudster, accused of irregularities in U.S. government schemes, has been arrested in India, FBI Director Kash Patel said in Washington.
Manjit Singh Bedi, who allegedly defrauded the U.S. government of $6 lakh, had a bounty of $1.5 lakh on his head.
“Bedi was just arrested in India and was believed to have fled there sometime last year. The FBI is actively working to secure his return to the United States,” Mr. Patel said in a post on X.
According to the FBI, Mr. Bedi operated a small grocery store in Tacoma, Washington, and swiped customers' government benefits cards to give them cash instead of food under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Programme (SNAP).
“This is the 5th Most Wanted Fraudster captured since the creation of the new list three months ago – and yet another high-value target captured overseas. Subjects captured so far have been responsible for a combined over USD two billion in fraud and were on the run for almost 4,000 days collectively prior to arrest,” Mr. Patel said.
Mr. Bedi is charged with a series of offences including wire fraud, SNAP benefits fraud, and more, Mr. Patel said.
Instead of selling food to participants, Mr. Bedi allegedly swiped their Electronic Benefit Transfer cards and gave them cash, keeping half of the proceeds for himself, the FBI said on Thursday (September 3, 2026).
The FBI claimed that Mr. Bedi, a naturalised U.S. citizen, defrauded the U.S. government of at least $6 lakh between March 2024 and June 2025.
After being indicted for wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud, Mr. Bedi was allowed to appear in court without being arrested.
He was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state.
However, Mr. Bedi soon drove across the border to Canada and then fled to India, the FBI said.
A federal arrest warrant was issued for Bedi on May 21 in a U.S. district court after he was charged with Violations of Conditions of Supervision.

briefs.headline: ‘Aaj Sunday hai kya?’: Irfan Pathan trolls Pakistan after India’s crushing win
briefs.deck: In a dominating performance, India triumphed over Pakistan by seven wickets in the Women's Asia Cup 2026. The young spinners Shree Charani and Prema Rawat played pivotal roles in dismantling the Pakistan batting lineup, which mustered a mere 55 runs, their lowest in T20 history. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur celebrated a significant personal achievement, while Irfan Pathan humorously recalled his…
briefs.bodyText:
Irfan Pathan
 wasted little time taking a cheeky dig at Pakistan after India produced another one-sided victory over their arch-rivals in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 on Saturday.
Minutes after India crushed Pakistan by seven wickets in their Group A clash, the former India all-rounder took to X with a four-word post that quickly went viral.
Irfan Pathan's post
“Aaj Sunday hai kya?” Pathan wrote.
The post was a clear throwback to one of his most talked-about social media jibes from last year, when he repeatedly mocked Pakistan after India defeated the Men in Green in three T20Is played on consecutive Sundays.
On that occasion, Pathan had posted, “Sunday kaisa raha padosiyo,” after India's victories, turning the phrase into a recurring taunt aimed at Pakistan.
India spin twins leave Pakistan in tatters
Pathan’s latest post came after India completely dominated Pakistan in the Women’s Asia Cup encounter, with young spinners Shree Charani and Prema Rawat playing the starring roles.
Pakistan were bowled out for just 55 in 18.1 overs, their lowest-ever total in T20 cricket. India’s spin attack dismantled the Pakistan batting line-up after 
Harmanpreet Kaur
 opted to introduce her spinners once she realised the pitch was offering turn.
Charani, a 22-year-old left-arm orthodox spinner, finished with impressive figures of 3/7 from four overs, while 24-year-old leg-spinner Prema Rawat claimed 3/9 in her four overs.
Shafali Verma chipped in with 1/10 from three overs before Deepti Sharma wrapped things up with 2/5 in 3.1 overs.
Pakistan had initially looked comfortable, reaching 27 without losing a wicket in just over four overs. Muneeba Ali made 13 and Shawaal Zulfiqar scored 14, but their dismissals triggered a spectacular collapse.
Pakistan lost six wickets for only nine runs to slump to 36/6 after 10 overs.
India's bowlers also produced 78 dot balls during Pakistan's 18.1-over innings, leaving the opposition with virtually no room to recover.
Harmanpreet creates history before sealing win
The match was also a landmark occasion for Harmanpreet Kaur, who became the first international captain, male or female, to lead India in 150 T20Is.
She marked the achievement with a commanding bowling display from her team and then finished the chase herself, hitting the winning six down the ground.
India reached the target in only 8.4 overs despite losing Shafali Verma for 12, 
Smriti Mandhana
 for nine and Pratika Rawal for four.
Harmanpreet remained unbeaten on 18, while Deepti Sharma finished on 12 not out as India completed another emphatic victory over Pakistan.
The result further underlined India's dominance in the Women's T20 Asia Cup. India have now won seven of their eight matches against Pakistan in the tournament's history, with Pakistan's only victory coming once.
And with India cruising to victory long before the scheduled finish, Pathan's “Aaj Sunday hai kya?” quickly became the perfect social media punchline to another completely one-sided India-Pakistan contest.

briefs.headline: Kempegowda tower poses heritage hitch to tunnel road project
briefs.deck: Kempegowda tower poses heritage hitch to tunnel
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The over four-century-old Kempegowda watchtower, a landmark of Bengaluru’s early history, has emerged as a fresh concern in the 17.65-km north-south tunnel road project which is proposed beneath Lalbagh. An expert committee -- constituted by the Geological Survey of India (GSI) -- has warned that tunnelling and excavation could cause cracks or displacement of the tower as well as the ancient rock..“As the ramps and tunnel boring machine (TBM) shaft are planned close to Lalbagh rock and the Kempegowda watchtower, tunnelling and excavation beneath or adjacent to the rock can redistribute stresses and may induce small displacements or cracking in the rock mass,” the 27-page report states, warning of potential long-term structural damage..On Page 18 of the report, the GSI expert committee has specifically stated that the proximity of the historic Kempegowda watchtower on the crest of the monument “amplifies the concern”. “Displacements of the rock could affect both the geotechnical and structural stability of the monument rock and this heritage landmark.”.The watchtower is itself a four-century-old landmark, with some historical accounts dating it back to 1537, while others believe it was constructed in 1606. Karnataka Tourism, a government website, describes it as a 16th-century structure built by Kempegowda I, the founder of Bengaluru..'Tunnel may damage Lalbagh rock, widen cracks': GSI expert committee flags risks.Any suggestion that a major road project could threaten a landmark bearing Kempegowda’s name could therefore prove politically sensitive. It is more so for the state government, especially Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who has announced a slew of initiatives to honour the legacy of Kempegowda, regarded as the founder of Bengaluru, in the last three years..The GSI has stopped short of saying the tower will be damaged. Its concern is about risks posed by vibration, excavation, stress redistribution and possible cracking, particularly because of the tower’s location atop the monument..The committee has recommended an independent technical review of the location of TBM Shaft 4 to maximise its setback from the protected monument before the construction begins..As DH reported on September 4, the report also recommended additional geotechnical investigations while noting that groundwater drawdown, construction vibration and potential fracturing have implications for the stability of the National Geological Monument..Historian Suresh Moona said the Kempegowda tower is “not a simple structure” and has a significant historical background linked to Bengaluru’s culture and heritage. “There is a perception that the Kempegowda towers marked the boundaries of Bengaluru. It is not so. When Kempegowda built Bengaluru, it was prosperous. The envious landlords of surrounding villages wanted to attack the city. Historically speaking, it was Kempegowda II who built these towers for security purposes. These watchtowers are situated on the elevated region and by the side of highways,” he said. The tower, he said, also became an insignia of the Bengaluru City Corporation.

briefs.headline: Police probe into fraud claims for Bidadi compensation
briefs.deck: Probe into fraud claims for Bidadi compensation
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The police have launched an investigation into fraudulent attempts to claim compensation for land being acquired for the proposed Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township after revenue officials came across allegedly forged documents in two applications..The Bidadi police registered two cases on September 3, following complaints by the special land acquisition officer, Greater Bengaluru Development Authority (GBDA), after a scrutiny of compensation claims exposed suspected fake seals, signatures and genealogy certificates..The state government recently issued a final notification to acquire lands across several villages near Bidadi. The GBDA office has been receiving and processing compensation applications from local landowners daily, according to the FIR..The fraudulent attempts, which involved a total claim of more than Rs 5 crore, unravelled on September 2 when applicants submitted consent forms for land parcels in Aralalusandra village..‘Will judges who fixed Rs 12 crore for resort karab land fix similar amount for Bidadi farmers?'.In the first case, accused Shankara Reddy S and Krishna Reddy S submitted documents claiming compensation for Survey No 28/5 consisting of 1 acre 1 gunta. In the second case, Venkatesh H and Rajashekar H submitted forms for Survey No 43/1 consisting of 37 guntas along with identity documents of two women, Manjula and Sujatha..The submitted documents contained family tree certificates bearing the digital signature of the Bidadi Hobli deputy tahsildar, alongside photo and signature attestation letters purportedly issued by the village administrative officer (VAO) of Kanchugaranahalli..Suspecting foul play upon preliminary physical inspection of the documents, GBDA officials alerted the Ramanagara tahsildar and additional deputy commissioner for verification on September 3..An internal probe by the revenue department confirmed that the Kanchugaranahalli VAO had never issued any landowner verification letters, declaring the seals and signatures entirely forged..Also, when officials cross-checked the revenue reference (RD) numbers printed on the family tree certificates against the state's Nada Kacheri software database, the system revealed that RD numbers actually belonged to routine caste and income certificates rather than family tree documents. The tahsildar reported that only land revenue receipts had been legitimately issued for the survey numbers in question. ."The accused are reportedly from Dobbaspet and are not farmers from the vicinity," a senior police officer at the Bidadi police station told DH. The police are investigating further details about the accused and their backgrounds..Based on the complaints, the Bidadi police registered cases against the accused under Sections 318(4) (cheating), 336(3) (forgery), 319(2) (impersonation) and 3(5) (joint criminal liability) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023..The police have launched an investigation to track down the accused and uncover if an organised racket is fabricating revenue documents to siphon off compensation funds..Yashavantha T, state general secretary of the Karnataka Prantha Raitha Sangha, lashed out at the authorities and the administration.."This police complaint stands as proof that the acrobatics staged by the GBDA and the state government aimed at concealing the fact that a majority of farmers are opposing the Bidadi Township project, while falsely portraying that landowners are coming forward voluntarily to receive compensation has only benefited fraudsters and thieves who forge documents to loot compensation funds." .A local farmer told DH that "people prepare family tree documents for land compensation, but they intentionally leave out their own brothers and sisters just to pocket the whole government payout themselves".."When sisters complain, middlemen intervene, warning them they will get nothing unless they take a tiny fraction like five lakhs instead of fifty. Family trust is weaponised, sons hide money from fathers and brothers steal signatures. If a landowner refuses to yield, agents scout distant relatives to file fake lawsuits. They pressure owners, saying, accept less now or court stays will leave you with zero. It’s pure blackmail, just like politicians exploiting weaknesses," the farmer, who didn't want to be identified, said.

briefs.headline: Congress will launch 100-day OBC rights campaign: Koppula Raju
briefs.deck: Koppula Raju said the slogan raised by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi during his Bharat Jodo Yatra had evolved into a movement and that Telangana had emerged as a “role model” in conducting a scientific caste survey under Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.
briefs.bodyText:
The Congress will launch a 100-day campaign for OBC rights across Telangana, demanding an immediate nationwide caste census and removal of the 50% ceiling on reservations, Congress Working Committee invitee Koppula Raju said on Saturday.
Speaking at Gandhi Bhavan along with Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar and TPCC president, Mr. Mahesh Kumar Goud, he said the slogan raised by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi during his Bharat Jodo Yatra had evolved into a movement and that Telangana had emerged as a “role model” in conducting a scientific caste survey under Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.
Mr. Raju said the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and party president Mallikarjun Kharge had been pressing Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the last five years to conduct a caste census along with the population census. The party now intended to turn the demand into a nationwide movement, he said.
He alleged that while Mr. Modi had announced that an OBC caste census would be conducted along with the population census, the Centre had not included an OBC enumeration in the census process. Union Home Minister Amit Shah had also stated in Parliament that an OBC caste census would be undertaken along with the family survey, but the relevant forms did not contain a provision for OBC enumeration, Mr. Raju claimed.
He contrasted this with Telangana’s caste survey, stating that the State government had consulted OBC caste associations and identified 134 OBC communities. “A proper OBC enumeration was conducted in Telangana,” he said.

stories.headline: Lokayukta registers suo motu case over lack of medical aid at Shivajinagar bus stand
stories.deck: The action was initiated by Justice K.N. Phaneendra, Upalokayukta, Karnataka.
stories.bodyText:
Close on the heels of Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh sitting among passengers, hearing their complaints directly and ordering immediate action over the absence of a doctor at a Namma Clinic and delays in issuing student bus passes, the Karnataka Lokayukta has registered a suo motu case against a BMTC official over the failure to provide timely medical assistance to an elderly passenger at Shivajinagar bus stand.
The case has been registered against Chandrakala, Assistant Traffic Manager, Shivajinagar BMTC Bus Stand (TTMC), following a newspaper report highlighting how an elderly passenger who collapsed inside a bus and allegedly remained without medical assistance for more than 30 minutes.
The action was initiated by Justice K.N. Phaneendra, Upalokayukta, Karnataka.
The passenger had reportedly boarded a BMTC bus at Ramamurthy Nagar and travelled to Shivajinagar. On reaching the bus stand, he reportedly suffered a seizure and became unresponsive. Though the bus had reached its destination, the driver and conductor allegedly struggled for more than 30 minutes to get him out of the vehicle.
The incident occurred despite the Commercial Street Police Station being around 100 metres away and Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital located nearby.
Journalists present at the bus stand subsequently called the emergency number 112 seeking assistance. The police initially suggested that the passenger be taken to Bowring Hospital in the BMTC bus, but the driver reportedly expressed his inability to do so.
The passenger was eventually brought out of the bus and handed over to the police. The bus subsequently resumed its journey.
The Upalokayukta observed that passengers are entitled to basic facilities at bus stands, including access to medical assistance during emergencies.
The order referred to Article 41 of the Constitution, which places an obligation on the State to improve public health, and the Supreme Court’s wider interpretation of Article 21, which includes the right to live with dignity and access to healthcare.
Apart from naming the Assistant Traffic Manager as the respondent, the Upalokayukta directed the managing director of BMTC to examine the shortcomings and take appropriate corrective measures.
The BMTC managing director has specifically been directed to examine the need for providing medical facilities at all BMTC bus stands in Bengaluru and submit a report on the action taken.
The matter has been posted for October 12, 2026.

stories.headline: SIR hearings descend into confusion and chaos on Day 1 in Bengaluru
stories.deck: While some voters had come to collect their notices, many did not know what a “logical discrepancy” meant, why their name had been marked as “not mapped” or what they were expected to prove.
stories.bodyText:
On the first day of hearing for voters in Bengaluru under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), some questions were commonly heard in the single-room offices of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) across multiple centres -- “Can you give me my notice?”, “Is my name there?”, “What documents do I have to show?”...
While some had come to collect their notices, many did not know what a “logical discrepancy” meant or why their name had been marked as “not mapped” or what they were expected to prove.
At a BBMP ward office in C.V. Raman Nagar constituency, 82-year-old wheelchair-bound Selva Raj had arrived with three photocopies each of his Aadhaar and ration card. He had assumed these documents would help establish that he had been living in and voting from the same constituency, against his notice flagged for “no mapping”. Mr. Selva Raj did not know that they were not among the 11 accepted documents.
“This is no less than mental harassment,” he said, pointing to the wheelchair.
The hearing across the city left voters — particularly the elderly who struggled to reach the venue and those who were clueless about the process — scrambling to understand what they had to do, and exposed the lack of awareness among the public.
At hearing venues in C.V. Raman Nagar, Cox Town and parts of Central Bengaluru visited by The Hindu, people and BLOs were equally anxious and confused.
Within the small space occupied by at least 100 voters at Cox Town BBMP ward office, people were pushing past each other to find their names on the list of voters issued notices and show them to their BLO. Many did not know that they first had to establish that their name was on the list before approaching the BLO.
At another venue in Cox Town, the BLO was left scanning notices while also trying to locate the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) who was supposed to conduct the hearings. The AERO was nowhere to be found as voters waited. At another venue in the same area, an AERO himself was seen struggling with the scanning process.
Many voters, like Samar Halarnkar, son of a former IPS officer, could not even get a copy of their notice amid the overwhelming crowd. Mr. Halarnkar and his 90-year-old mother had received notices for a hearing later this month. Like many others, he thought that the process was over and that their names were secure because they appeared in the draft rolls.
However, he learnt about the notice through a WhatsApp group and had to go himself to get a copy, though the process states that BLOs should serve the notice and click and upload a photograph of it.
The college where the two are expected to appear for the hearing is at the end of a dug-up lane accessible only by two-wheelers, he said, arguing that there was no chance his 90-year-old, wheelchair-bound mother could get there.
No idea about documents
Much like during the enumeration phase, confusion over documents persisted. Many voters said they had no idea which documents to carry. “We thought the process would be similar to enumeration, but this time only physical verification would be done, where BLOs would check the form and ask for Aadhaar, PAN or ration card,” David, a voter from Indiranagar, said.
Many voters the The Hindu met said they did not have birth certificates, let alone passports. Several women said they had no documents, including Aadhaar.
Senior journalist T.M. Veera Raghav, who accompanied a family member to a hearing venue in Kengeri, described the process as cumbersome and said that if done this way, it would result in many people missing out on the hearings. While BLOs were helpful, he said, many people did not even know why they had been served notices, as the notices were only in Kannada.
Karnataka CEO V. Anbu Kumar had said that notices would be served in Kannada and one more language as per regional need — English and Kannada for Bengaluru and Marathi and Kannada for Belagavi, for instance. However, voters have so far received notices only in Kannada.

briefs.headline: Civic workers skipping duty to face dismissal: Krishna Byre Gowda
briefs.deck: A statement issued by the Karnataka State Municipal Workers’ Union notes that Krishna Byre Gowda’s should not turn allegations of individual dereliction of duty into collective humiliation
briefs.bodyText:
Civic workers who routinely remain absent from duty will face dismissal from service, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Saturday.
Speaking after a meeting with MPs, MLAs, and MLCs on civic issues at Vidhana Soudha, Mr. Gowda said nearly 30% of civic workers deployed at various locations were not reporting for duty regularly.
“Three notices will be issued to workers who fail to attend duty. If they do not respond to the notices, action will be initiated to dismiss them from service as per the rules,” he said.
Mr. Gowda said door-to-door garbage collection was a primary responsibility of civic workers and that absenteeism was contributing directly to the emergence of new garbage black spots.
“If 30% of civic workers do not report for work every day, how can we keep the city clean?” he asked.
New waste management plan
A total of 33 waste management packages have been formulated, of which 21 have received approval. The process of issuing work orders to contractors is under way, and they have been directed to commence operations within two months, Mr. Gowda said.
Under the new system, existing auto-tippers with a capacity of around one tonne will be replaced with vehicles capable of carrying three tonnes of waste. The GPS tracking will be mandatory, with each vehicle assigned a designated route that it must follow every day.
“The city currently has the capacity to collect around 5,200 tonnes of waste a day. This will be increased to about 9,000 tonnes a day under the new system,” the Minister said.
He stressed that every household would have waste collected at its doorstep, and those unable to hand over waste at the designated time can keep garbage bags on their compound wall or grill, from where collection staff will pick it up.
Mr. Gowda said a public awareness campaign would be launched to familiarise citizens with the new waste-disposal system.
Meanwhile, the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has engaged contractors to remove abandoned and unused vehicles from public spaces. The Minister urged elected representatives to monitor the process in their areas and report problems to officials. He also asked local representatives to monitor garbage clearance and the cleaning of private vacant sites.
Union condemns
However, the Karnataka State Municipal Workers’ Union has condemned Mr. Gowda’s remarks of 30% absenteeism. The union alleged that such remarks reflected a feudal mindset and said the Minister’s conduct should be condemned by the public.
“If that (absenteeism) is the case, what are the supervisors doing? Action should be taken against those who are not working. Instead, it is not right to make remarks that insult everyone,” said Syed Mujeeb, general secretary of the union.
The statement said a Minister should not turn allegations of individual dereliction of duty into collective humiliation.

briefs.headline: B-to-A Khata conversion rebate window ends with 80,412 applications; only 12% of total beneficiaries
briefs.deck: Bengaluru North City Corporation received the highest number of applications at 23,354, generating ₹144.9 crore in revenue
briefs.bodyText:
Despite a 60% rebate on B-to-A Khata conversion charges, a meagre 12% of the estimated beneficiaries have applied for the conversion.
By the time the rebate window ended on August 23, the corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) had received 80,412 applications, while the revised estimate of the total number of properties stood at over 7 lakh.
According to GBA data, the applications received have generated a total of ₹525.7 crore in revenue for the corporations. One of the corporation commissioners told The Hindu that many applications are still under review and that the revenue would go up.
Bengaluru North City Corporation received the highest number of applications at 23,354, generating ₹144.9 crore in revenue. It was followed by the west corporation with 22,479 applications and a revenue of ₹131.1 crore and the south corporation with 17,262 applications, which generated ₹124.3 crore.
According to the GBA officials, the north and west corporations also have a larger number of B-Khata properties, which is why they have received more applications.
Rebate spurs takers
When the rebate was announced, the conversion charge was set at 5% of the guidance value in the area, which meant property owners had to spend lakhs of rupees, making it unattractive.
Fewer than 14,000 applications were received in the first few months. The government subsequently announced a discount by reducing the conversion charge to 2% of the guidance value.
A corporation commissioner said that even with the rebate, the scheme did not attract much interest initially, but gained substantial momentum in the last nine days of the discount window. Until August 14, about 48,000 applications had been received. In the next nine days, however, 32,000 applications flooded the corporations.
When asked whether the rebate scheme would be extended considering the last-minute surge, the officials said there were currently no discussions about it.
“The properties for which we have received most applications are also in places where the guidance value is relatively less, which means many are still contemplating the scheme. We also have cases where owners have applied for conversion and checked the charges, eventually retreating and not paying the charges,” the official added.
One of the major setbacks to the scheme is that the conversion would regularise the property or site, but would not automatically regularise buildings constructed on it.
Corporations not on board with another rebate
According to the GBA sources, the corporations are not interested in announcing rebates again, citing the drop in revenue. For instance, the north corporation’s 2026-27 budget outlay was over ₹4,300 crore, of which ₹680 crore was estimated to come from the B-to-A conversions. Similarly, other corporations had also made substantial revenue estimates, which have now taken a hit.

briefs.headline: One year on, how has the Greater Bengaluru Authority fared?
briefs.deck: Restructuring of the civic body was envisaged to address micro-level issues through decentralisation of the administration
briefs.bodyText:
In this six-part series, The Hindu’s reporters evaluate the restructuring of urban governance in the city with the Greater Bengaluru Authority and five corporations, a year after the reform.
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), which completed a year after replacing the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) with five city corporations, increased the number of wards from 198 to 369. But while 171 new wards were added to the civic map, there has been no corresponding expansion of facilities such as primary health centres (PHCs), Indira Canteens or even ward offices, the local touchpoints through which the five-corporation system was expected to bring civic services closer to residents.
The restructuring was also envisaged to address micro-level issues through decentralisation of the administration. But city corporations are still mostly working with a workforce deployed for the old 198-ward setup and not upgraded to the 369 wards yet. Moreover, the vacancy rate is around 40%. This essentially means, the intended benefits of the new governance structure is yet to reach citizens.
Residents have pointed to continuing gaps in areas such as solid waste management, funding, and execution. With elections long overdue and councillors and ward committees yet to be in place, many feel the new administrative structure can deliver its full promise of bringing governance closer to citizens only when there is a stronger local accountability mechanism.
According to GBA sources, top-level coordination and frequent meetings have particularly helped expedite long-delayed civic works and infrastructure projects. However, problems faced by people on a daily basis, such as garbage blackspots, waste collection, potholes, and citizen services persist.
The new corporations had high hopes for three major sources: advertisement revenue, premium FAR, and B-Khata to A-Khata conversion. However, the new setup will step into another year with revenue capacities largely unchanged.
The corporations are grappling with shortage of staff, offices and funds, while key institutions meant to drive the city’s development and planning, such as the Economic Development Agency and the Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC), are far from becoming functional.

briefs.headline: A year into GBA, Bengaluru still awaits key governance institutions
briefs.deck: The corporations are grappling with shortage of staff, offices and funds, while key institutions meant to drive the city’s development and planning, such as the Economic Development Agency and the Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee, are far from becoming functional
briefs.bodyText:
A year after the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) came into effect, Bengaluru has five city corporations headed by separate commissioners, but much of the governance structure envisaged for the city is still incomplete.
The corporations are grappling with shortage of staff, offices and funds, while key institutions meant to drive the city’s development and planning, such as the Economic Development Agency and the Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC), are far from becoming functional.
The Greater Bengaluru Governance Act mandated an Economic Development Agency within a year of the GBA’s constitution to attract investment and promote employment in the Greater Bengaluru area, including through Public Private Partnerships. Yet, even as the corporations are looking for ways to strengthen their own revenue base, the agency meant to drive economic development at the metropolitan level is yet to be established.
The BMPC, which was intended to bring together plans at different levels and prepare a development plan for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Area, has also remained non-functional. Meanwhile, with elections to the five corporations repeatedly postponed, ward committees, the institutional mechanism for citizen participation and monitoring of local works, are yet to be constituted.
Experts said that, so far, the changes have largely been administrative, without the institutions needed to make the new system work.
According to civic activist Kathyayini Chamaraj, the absence of elected local bodies has meant that the participatory mechanisms envisaged under the constitutional amendment have remained largely dysfunctional.
Ms. Chamaraj argued that nodal officers were appointed in place of councillors to conduct informal ward committee meetings, but these could not serve the purpose of institutionalised citizen participation. The Area Sabhas, through which voters could participate in governance at the local level and which existed under the BBMP Act, 2020, have also been dropped from the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, she said.
The absence of an elected local government has also affected metropolitan-level planning, Ms. Chamaraj said. “The BMPC was meant to collate plans prepared at the ward level and prepare a draft development plan for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Area. Instead, the planning function had effectively been centralised with the GBA.”
The gaps in the planning system become more significant as the government begins work on a new GIS-based Comprehensive Master Plan for Greater Bengaluru with a long-term 2047 vision. The plan is only now moving forward, even as major infrastructure projects are being planned and taken up.
Ashish Verma, convener of the IISc Sustainable Transportation Lab (IST Lab), said a comprehensive master plan would have ensured that these projects – elevated corridors, short tunnels, long tunnels, which are also causing a lot of damage to ecology and environment, would have been studied in totality and in a holistic planning framework before being finalised and tendered out.
In the absence of such a framework, decisions were being taken ‘reactively‘ without first assessing what the project would actually solve and its impact on land use, land prices and accessibility, Mr. Verma argued.
The issue also raises questions about the functioning of the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA), which was envisaged as a coordinating and scrutiny body for major transport projects. Recent changes to its framework, including provisions allowing deemed approval in certain cases, have raised concerns among urban experts about the extent of scrutiny available for large projects such as tunnel roads and elevated corridors.
Meanwhile, the five corporations are themselves yet to acquire the administrative capacity needed to function effectively.
Urbanist Ashwin Mahesh said that while the government had made administrative changes, the government had not followed through with the staffing and infrastructure required for them to function. He pointed to the recent changes with the BMLTA as an example of governance moving backwards rather than forwards, arguing that an institution that was supposed to strengthen coordination in transport planning had instead been made “toothless”.
Mr. Mahesh said the city had effectively lost a year in implementing the changes people expected from the GBA. “Whatever you ask, they (GBA) are saying we are about to do it or we are in the process of doing it,” he said, pointing to pending ward offices, garbage tracking, road-quality improvements and other measures. He argued that the government could not rely entirely on an already understaffed bureaucracy to monitor every civic issue and needed to build systems through which public could participate in identifying and monitoring problems.
(Series concludes)

stories.headline: Coal production re-accelerates amid easing monsoon; daily output rises to 1.7 MT
stories.deck: Coal India’s sizeable inventory position as a cushion against supply disruptions. The improvement in production and dispatch amid easing monsoon offers greater flexibility, supporting higher supplies to power sector.
stories.bodyText:
Coal production at mines operated by state-owned Coal India Ltd is gaining momentum as intense monsoon rains ease across coal-bearing regions, the Union Coal Ministry said on Saturday.
Average daily production rose to around 1.7 million tonnes (MT) on September 4, against approximately 1.36 MT a day during the first three rain-affected days of the month, according to the ministry.
The improvement comes as declining rainfall allows mining operations and coal handling to normalise.
“Coal beds that had turned sticky and wet following prolonged exposure to rain are now drying, making freshly mined coal more free-flowing and easier to transfer, handle and dispatch through Coal Handling Plants (CHPs),” it said.
The ministry further stated that overburden removal—a key indicator of exposure in a coal bed, involving the removal of layers of soil, rock and other material to access the coal—also increased to 4.1 million cubic metres on September 4, compared with 2.5 million cubic metres recorded during the first three days of the month.
Kolkata-headquartered miner and its subsidiaries have also offered power plants with existing supply agreements the option to lift additional coal beyond their annual contracted quantities through road transport, alongside existing rail-based supplies, the ministry said.
“With dry spells setting in, loading is expected to pick up further over the coming days. Close monitoring is being maintained to sustain this trend,” the ministry said.
Coal availability for the power sector has also strengthened. Average daily dispatch to power plants increased to 1.5 MT on September 4, from around 1.35 MT a day during the first three days of September, the ministry said.
The government also highlighted Coal India’s sizeable inventory position as a cushion against supply disruptions. The miner currently has around 76 MT of coal stocked at its pitheads, including 46 MT of coal ready for extraction, it said.

stories.headline: Son loses gifted flat after neglecting parents; why he may still inherit it later
stories.deck: A recent Bombay High Court case involved a son who was directed to vacate his father’s flat after the court found that he had failed to honour the condition attached to the gift of the property. The flat had been transferred to him on the understanding that he would take care of his parents, an obligation he did not fulfil.
stories.bodyText:
A couple gifted their son a flat that they had bought in 2005 on the condition that he take care of them. Years later, the Bombay High Court directed the son to vacate the flat. Here’s what the case is about.
A recent Bombay High Court case involved a son who was directed to vacate his father’s flat after the court found that he had failed to honour the condition attached to the gift of the property. The flat had been transferred to him on the understanding that he would take care of his parents, an obligation he did not fulfil.
Why court ordered eviction
The Bombay High Court considered Section 23 of the Senior Citizens Act, which provides that where a senior citizen transfers property subject to a condition that the transferee will provide for their basic physical needs and the transferee subsequently fails to do so, the transfer can be treated as having been made by fraud or coercion and can be cancelled.
Shrusti Shah, Associate Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the gift deed executed when the parents transferred the flat to their son specifically required him to look after them in all respects in the future.
In other words, the responsibility was not merely an informal expectation between the parents and their son. It was expressly incorporated as a condition in the gift deed.
Shah pointed out: “Here, both parts of that test were met: there was a clear condition in the deed, and the relationship broke down so badly that the parents actually had to leave their own home.”
There is a specific safeguard available when parents want to transfer property to a child while making the child responsible for their care. Section 23 provides a legal mechanism in such circumstances.
Shah explains that when a gift is made subject to the condition that the child will take care of the senior citizen parents, failure to honour that commitment can provide a legal basis for taking the property back. That is what happened in the Bombay High Court case.
Proper documentation and registration can also be particularly important for senior citizen parents. The Bombay High Court judgment demonstrates the importance of recording the terms of a property transfer clearly, rather than relying on verbal assurances or claims made later.
But, this raises another important question: after the gift deed has been cancelled and the son has been ordered to vacate the property, does he retain any inheritance rights in the flat?
Son’s inheritance rights
In the Bombay High Court case, the parents were senior citizens with sons and daughters. After getting married, the son began living with his wife in his parents’ Lower Parel flat. The property was the self-acquired asset of his father, who was a Hindu male, making the Hindu Succession Act applicable to the case.
For others, the Indian Succession Act applies.
Shah explained that once a gift deed is cancelled under Section 23, the legal position is that the transfer is treated as though it had not taken place. The property therefore returns to the parents.
Since the Lower Parel flat was purchased by the parents in 2005 and was not inherited property that had passed down through the family, the son does not acquire any birthright in it while his parents are still alive.
Shah says: “Under Hindu law, self-acquired property is for the owners’ to do with as they please.”
According to Shah, the son could inherit the Lower Parel flat only after the death of his parents. Even then, if the parents have not left a Will, he would inherit the property along with his mother and sisters as a Class I heir. Alternatively, the parents could choose to leave the property to him through a Will.
When does a Hindu son have inheritance rights?
The Bombay High Court case involved a self-acquired property belonging to Hindu parents. The position, however, is different when the property is ancestral Hindu property.
Shah says: “If it's ancestral property, meaning something that's been passed down through the male line without being divided, then yes, a son has a right to it simply by being born into the family. Interestingly, since 2005, daughters have that same right too.”
A self-acquired property, such as the flat in this case that the parents purchased with their own money, is treated differently. The son does not have an automatic entitlement to such a property. Shah says: “He'd only inherit it if his parents die without a will, in which case succession law kicks in, or if they specifically choose to give it to him in a Will.”
Therefore, the nature of the property is the first thing that determines whether a son has a claim over it. Where the property is self-acquired, the parents’ own decision, including whether they leave behind a Will, becomes important.
Can his inheritance be prevented?
Senior citizen parents generally have greater control over self-acquired property than over ancestral property.
Shah says: “Self-acquired property doesn't automatically pass to children while the parents are alive or even necessarily after if the parent has executed a Will or a gift deed disinheriting the son or daughter.”
A Will can therefore determine how the self-acquired property is distributed rather than leaving the property to be divided according to the default succession rules, Shah said.
Shah says: “Parents can also just go ahead and transfer or gift the property to someone else during their lifetime, as long as it's done freely and without conditions attached, because once a transfer is unconditional, it generally can't be undone.”

stories.headline: Global food prices rise 1.9%, says UN body; highest since 2022 amid weather, war disruptions
stories.deck: Food prices worldwide hit the highest levels since late 2022 in August, fueled by unpredictable weather conditions and rising geopolitical conflicts. These factors, coupled with interruptions to trade pathways, are raising alarms over the supply of vital commodities. This troubling update was shared by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization on Friday, underscoring the increasing vulnerabilities…
stories.bodyText:
World food prices rose to their highest level since late 2022 in August as extreme weather, geopolitical tensions and disruptions to trade routes heightened concerns over supplies of key agricultural commodities, the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) said on Friday.
The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 133.3 points in August, up from a revised 130.8 in July. The reading was the highest since November 2022, though it remained nearly 17 per cent below the record reached in March 2022 following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, reported Reuters.
Prices of cereals, vegetable oils, sugar, meat and dairy all increased during the month. Grain prices climbed to a three-year high, while sugar prices reached their highest level in more than a year.
“August’s increase in global food prices is a warning that the risk premium is returning to food markets: climate shocks, geopolitical tensions and disrupted trade logistics are converging to tighten supply expectations,” FAO chief economist Maximo Torero said.
Weather, wars drive supply concerns
Extreme heat and drought in Europe have raised concerns over maize and sugar beet harvests and livestock production. 
At the same time, the anticipated El Nino weather pattern has fuelled fears of lower palm oil and sugar output in Asia.
The ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine has also disrupted agricultural trade, with intensified attacks in the Black Sea curtailing grain shipments from the two major exporters. Meanwhile, the US-Iran conflict has put additional pressure on fertiliser flows, potentially affecting crop production.
The FAO's cereal price index rose 2.2 per cent in August from the previous month, reaching its highest level since May 2024. The vegetable oil index increased 0.6 per cent to its highest since June 2022.
Sugar recorded the sharpest increase among the major food categories, with its benchmark jumping 11.9% to the highest level since June 2025. Lower production in Brazil's key centre-south region, along with weather concerns in Europe and Asia, contributed to the rise.
Global cereal output forecast cut
In a separate report, the FAO cut its forecast for global cereal production in 2026 by 3.4 million metric tons from its July estimate to 2.980 billion tons.
The revised forecast is 2% below 2025 production, marking the largest annual decline since 2018. However, output would still be the second-highest on record.
The agency also lowered its forecast for global cereal stocks at the end of the 2026/27 season by 1.1% to 947.2 million tons. The revised stock level is only marginally above the previous season.
A reduction in coarse grain stocks outweighed an upward revision to wheat inventories. The FAO said the higher wheat estimate reflected expectations of stockpiling in Russia and Ukraine as shipping disruptions hamper exports.

briefs.headline: Coal Ministry rejects ‘No Takers’ claim, says TFL, NTPC apply for gasification scheme
briefs.deck: Talcher Fertilisers Ltd is already working on implementing a coal-based ammonia-urea gasification complex, expected to be commissioned in FY 2027-28.
briefs.bodyText:
The Ministry of Coal on Saturday rejected reports that the Centre’s coal gasification incentive scheme had failed to attract applicants, saying Talcher Fertilisers Ltd (TFL) and NTPC Ltd have already submitted their applications ahead of the September 7 deadline.

TFL, a joint venture involving Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilisers, Coal India, GAIL and Fertiliser Corporation of India, is already implementing a coal-based ammonia-urea gasification complex in Talcher, Odisha. The project has an estimated investment of ₹13,277 crore and is expected to be commissioned in FY28.
The ministry said several other prospective applicants are also in communication with it, with their projects at various stages of preparation and application finalisation.
To facilitate participation in capital-intensive gasification projects, the government has adopted a rolling-round mechanism for applications. Once the current application window closes, the next round will open the following day and remain available for two months.
“The rolling-round mechanism has been deliberately incorporated in view of the substantial preparation and investment requirements associated with large-scale coal/lignite gasification projects,” the ministry said.

briefs.headline: 5G’s bigger opportunity lies in industrial automation, telecom executives say
briefs.deck: 4G is sufficient for many consumer uses, while private 5G could connect robots, machines and factory systems, but industrial adoption in India remains limited
briefs.bodyText:
India’s rapid rollout of 5G has brought the technology to millions of smartphone users, but its larger potential may lie in connecting machines, robots and industrial systems, telecom executives said.
Prathitha Muthurangam, Enterprise Business Head – Tamil Nadu & Kerala at Bharti Airtel, said 4G was adequate for many smartphone applications, while 5G could enable a broader range of industrial and machine-to-machine use cases.
“We don’t need 5G. Even 4G is enough for our phones to work,” she said, noting that smartphones do not utilise all the capabilities that 5G offers.
“But 5G as a data use case is for industries because it is a heavy duty,” she added, referring to industrial applications that require high-speed connectivity and low latency.
Muthurangam was speaking during a panel discussion on ‘5G & its Impact on Industrial Automation and Robotics’ at ASME’s International Mechanical Engineering Congress & Exposition (IMECE) in Chennai. The panel brought together executives from Bharti Airtel, Ericsson, KPMG, Nokia and Vodafone Idea.
According to the panelists, private 5G networks deployed within factories could connect machines, robots and industrial equipment through dedicated networks. Potential applications include automated guided vehicles (AGVs), autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), industrial Internet of Things (IoT), AI-powered visual inspection and edge computing.
Surendra Shenoy, Head of Design and Optimise, RAN Delivery at Nokia, said 5G represented a shift towards connectivity designed specifically for machines.
“5G was the first technology that was built for machines,” he said.
The low latency offered by 5G can enable machines to communicate and respond more quickly, which could be particularly important in industrial environments. The panelists noted that an AGV stopping unexpectedly during an operation, for example, could be more than a technical problem—it could become a safety concern.
Despite the potential, private 5G deployment in India remains at an early stage. Muthurangam said telecom companies had carried out several deployments, but the number was still relatively small.
“We’ve done a few deployments, but not large in numbers, but we are looking at a few more,” she said.
The panelists also noted that technology availability alone would not determine adoption. For manufacturers, the scale of investment required and the return generated by specific applications would be key factors in deciding whether to deploy private 5G networks.

briefs.headline: CBI books Subhash Chandra, others over alleged ₹1,322-crore loss to LIC Housing Finance
briefs.deck: The investigating agency alleges misrepresentation of facts and inflated net worth certificates submitted for loan approvals
briefs.bodyText:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a case against businessman Subhash Chandra and others for allegedly causing a wrongful loss of over ₹1,322 crore to LIC Housing Finance Limited (LICHFL) through misrepresentation of facts.
Those named in the First Information Report (FIR) include Mr. Chandra, Vasant Sagar Properties Private Limited and its director Pankaj Suroliya, Pan India Infrastructure Private Limited, Digital Subscriber Management and Consultancy Services Private Limited and its director Amish Pandya, Spirit Infrapower and Multiventures Private Limited and its director Rajeev Dholakia, and unidentified others.
LICHFL lodged a complaint with the agency on August 31, 2026, and the case was registered the same day. The complainant alleged that LICHFL had granted two credit facilities based on Mr. Chandra’s personal guarantees executed in 2018.
One loan of ₹500 crore was sanctioned for Vasant Sagar Properties Private Limited and Pan India Infraprojects Private Limited (co-borrower), and the second was of ₹480 crore to Digital Subscriber Management and Consultancy Services Private Limited and Spirit Infrapower and Multiventures Private Limited (co-borrower).
According to the FIR, the Vasant Sagar loan facility was granted based on a Net Worth Certificate submitted by Mr. Chandra, attesting that his net worth was ₹59,113.21 crore as on March 31, 2017. Another Net Worth Certificate, issued by a chartered accountancy firm on July 6, 2018, certified that his net worth was ₹40,562 crore.
The FIR alleged that in the course of subsequent proceedings under the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code for the personal insolvency resolution of Mr. Chandra, he categorically denied having the net worth stated in the certificates submitted to LICHFL for approval and disbursal of the loans.
In the course of proceedings, he allegedly stated that his net worth in 2024 was ₹31.79 crore and that even in 2017-18 he did not have a net worth of more than ₹40,000 crore. The agency’s complaint alleged that Mr. Chandra had, therefore, “colluded” with the borrowers to “defraud and cheat” LICHFL in advancing the loans to the borrower entities, which “misappropriated” the same.
LICHFL also accused Mr. Chandra of creating false documents to denote inflated and bogus net worth. “The accused persons have publicly disclosed their intention to leave India and are likely to do so, unless an FIR is registered and an investigation is undertaken at the earliest to trace the proceeds of the loan and assets of the accused persons,” said the complaint.
On August 25, a Bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) had approved a repayment plan requiring Mr. Chandra, chairman of the Essel Group, to pay ₹6.25 crore to settle his individual liability as a personal guarantor. The total admitted claim value stands at ₹22,006.57 crore against corporate debts.
However, on September 1, a five-member Bench of the Tribunal stayed the ruling and also barred Mr. Chandra from alienating his assets. The Essel Group chairman has opposed the formation of the five-member Bench to decide his personal insolvency case, arguing that the Tribunal does not have such a power.

briefs.headline: Crypto SIPs: How small-town millennials are increasingly dipping into crypto space
briefs.deck: From the thrill of overnight riches that drove the crypto craze in 2021, investors in India are maturing in the way they invest, and a new tool that reflects this maturity is the crypto SIP
briefs.bodyText:
The crypto sector in India is going through a transformation, with the get-rich-quick impulse of the young investors five years ago increasingly giving way to a more mature, systematic, and long-term attitude towards crypto investments. And this change can best be seen in the rise of a new type of crypto product: crypto Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs).
The crypto space in India is still unregulated and so finding official industry-wide data is impossible. However, each of the three of the largest crypto exchanges that The Hindu has spoken to have reported rapid growth in the adoption of crypto SIPs.
This shift does not involve small amounts either. According to calculations based on government data, more than ₹51,000 crore worth of crypto investments took place in India in 2024-25, the latest year for which there is data. By all accounts, this figure has grown significantly since then, and an increasing share is being routed through the SIP route.
Further, crypto SIPs are not a phenomenon limited to India’s metros. In fact, most of the activity is coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities and, as one crypto exchange put it, even from “Tier 10 cities”.
Rapid growth
“According to CoinDCX, around 20% of the people that were earlier investing in single crypto assets such as Bitcoin are now instead choosing crypto SIPs. This share was just 2-3%, or maximum 4%, as recently as nine months ago,” Mridul Gupta, Founding Partner of CoinDCX said.
Mr. Gupta pointed out how the current cohort of crypto investors choosing crypto SIPs is qualitatively different from those from five years ago when India experienced a crypto boom.
“Five years ago, we used to see a lot of sentiment around crypto for investing in tokens that were slightly new, slightly low priced, and being talked about in the social channels by influencers or in general in social media,” Mr. Gupta said. “Now we see the form of investment has changed from one-time buys to SIPs.”
“We see a lot of disciplined investment from a more mature audience now versus a GenZ kind of an audience,” he added. “In the last 3-6 months, our daily SIP creation at an absolute level has also gone up by 50-60%. It’s increasing at that pace every quarter or so.”
According to Prateek Gupta, Head of Business at Mudrex, over the last 12-18 months, the company has seen the Assets Under Management (AUM) through the SIP route grow almost 220% or nearly 3x.
Balaji Srihari, vice-president of the India Business at CoinSwitch also attested to the rapid growth in the SIP category.
“Between 2023-24 and 2025-26, active SIP users grew by around 75%, while the number of active SIPs increased by approximately 93%,” Mr. Srihari said. “Annual SIP inflows nearly doubled over the same period, and cumulative capital deployed through the SIP route rose by about 144%.”
He added that this trend intensified in particular in 2025-26, with active SIP users growing nearly 39% year-on-year and annual SIP inflows increasing by around 63%.
Long-term thinking
“This SIP trend has been so great in India in general,” Mr. Gupta of CoinDCX said. “Because people don’t want to time when they are investing, they don’t want to time the financial markets. They want to hedge the risk and be consistent and more disciplined in their investments. And that’s what we are really seeing pick up.”
He added that the cohort of crypto SIPs investors have a strong overlap with people who have already been investing systematically in mutual funds, gold, and even in stocks.
The way this works, Mr. Gupta from Mudrex explained, is a little different from how a normal autopay works in a mutual fund. For example, a user can deposit a bulk amount of ₹1 lakh on any crypto platform and set up a monthly SIP of ₹10,000 that will be debited from that amount every month. The corresponding crypto asset purchased each month will be deposited in the user’s wallet each month.
So, users not only accumulate crypto assets over time, but they benefit from any price increase that happens over this period.
“I think investors are figuring out that, as long as you are fundamentally bullish on a medium to long term basis on any asset, it is immaterial what your entry point is,” he explained.
Moving past youth & metros
According to CoinSwitch, the 26-35 years age group forms the largest segment of crypto SIP users, accounting for roughly 42-44% of users. Those aged 36-45 years account for around 28-31%, followed by the 18-25 years group at about 14-16%. Users aged 46 years and above represent roughly 12-13%.
“Around 17% of users are from Tier-1 cities, while approximately 31% are from Tier-2 cities and 52% are from Tier-3 cities,” Mr. Srihari added. “In other words, more than 80% of crypto SIP users come from non-metro markets, underlining the depth of adoption beyond large urban centres.” Both Mudrex and CoinDCX pointed to the same trend.
“You would be surprised by the kind of cities that we see a lot of participation from,” Mr. Gupta of Mudrex said. “They are not even like Tier 2, they are Tier 10! Even in small cities, people there are smart investors and want to be smart with their investment. People want to diversify their portfolio across multiple asset classes.”
According to CoinDCX, its crypto SIP users are heavily concentrated in the 27-28 years to 37-38 years category.
“This is very different from five years ago,” Mr. Gupta of CoinDCX said. “The 2021 crypto boom was largely led by the very young generation, the GenZ generation at that point in time, and a lot of speculation was there.”
What this means for regulation
“I think India’s regulatory approach will increasingly have to recognise that crypto has moved beyond a single use-case or investor profile,” Mr. Srihari said. “You now have long-term holders, active traders, exchanges, custodians and blockchain businesses, each presenting very different regulatory questions.”
“The government, therefore, has an opportunity to build an activity-based framework, where the intensity of oversight corresponds to the underlying risk, rather than putting the entire asset class into one regulatory bucket,” he added.
India’s regulatory bodies, however, remain less-than-keen to enter the crypto space. While they have not officially commented on the changing nature of crypto investments in India, officials have privately put forth their thoughts.
“We have been looking at crypto and the changes happening, but until the government decided whether it wants to classify cryptos as currencies or assets, there is little that we can do on this,” a senior official in the Securities and Exchange Board of India told The Hindu.
Officials in the Reserve Bank of India, too, said they have not changed their restrictive stance on private cryptos and their use in India.
