briefs.headline: When pets become premium customers
briefs.deck: Data released by imarc shows that the market size of pet care products reached 48.6 billion in 2025; it predicts a growth rate (CAGR) of 5.24% between 2026 and 2034
briefs.bodyText:
Bella gives the bowl a doubtful look. She takes a hesitant sniff of the pedigree food “served” before her, turns away and tosses it aside with immense disapproval.
For Tanvi, a journalist based in Bengaluru, this has become a familiar routine. Her Persian cat, Bella, refuses regular Pedigree cat food and waits impatiently for the more expensive fare to arrive in her abowl—the one that, apparently, smells right.
Bella’s preference is more than a fussy pet’s eating habit. It reflects a broader shift taking place in the pet-care market, where pet owners are increasingly willing to pay a premium for products they believe are better suited to their animals.
“A few years ago, expensive pedigree food like Royal Canin was a rarity and vanity in local pet shops,” says Renjith K.J., an amateur dog breeder. Today, however, premium brands such as Royal Canin have become increasingly common in pet stores, reflecting a growing appetite for high-end pet products.
The transformation accelerated during the COVID-19 pandemic, when pet ownership and spending on pets surged. A story published in The Hindu on July 25, 2026, highlighted how the pet industry boomed during the pandemic and underwent significant changes in the years that followed.
One of the most visible consequences has been the premiumisation of pet care. What was once considered an optional or indulgent expense is increasingly being treated as an essential part of pet ownership.
Pet insurance offers another example of this changing consumer mindset. Once an unfamiliar concept in India, pet insurance is gradually gaining attention as owners begin to view veterinary care and financial protection as part of responsible pet ownership.
The numbers point to a market with considerable room for growth. According to data from IMARC, the global pet-care products market reached $48.6 billion in 2025. The market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.24% between 2026 and 2034.
Medical expenditure
Dr. Soorej K., founder of Cochin Pet Hospital, Kerala’s first private multi-speciality veterinary hospital, says the changing culture of pet ownership has significantly influenced attitudes towards pet care.
“The shift in the culture of raising dogs has resulted in a change in the attitude towards pet care. Pet parents nowadays consider pets as family members,” he says.
This shift, he adds, has created a demand for more advanced and specialised treatment, which often comes at a higher cost.
“Expensive treatments like haemodialysis, laparoscopic surgery, keyhole animal birth control, etc., are offered nowadays for pets like dogs and cats. Pet parents specifically ask for these novel methods of healthcare,” Dr. Soorej says.
Healthcare for pets has become an increasingly expensive affair. Aswathi, a teacher from Kozhikode district in Kerala, lost her pet dog, Appu, to heart disease. Before his death, she had spent nearly ₹2 lakh on his treatment.
Although government veterinary hospitals offer several advanced treatments at significantly lower costs, various factors make them a second choice for many pet parents.
“Appu had a very serious heart disease and was prone to infections. From many of my friends’ experiences, I was sceptical about the cleanliness of government veterinary hospitals,” Aswathi says.
She also recalls struggling to find a government veterinary hospital during a late-night emergency, as many of them had already closed.
This is where pet insurance becomes relevant.
One of the major players in the sector, Bajaj Allianz, entered the pet insurance market in 2021. Amarnath Saxena, Chief Technical Officer of Bajaj General Insurance, says the company launched its product after observing that people were increasingly considering their pets part of the family.
“This shift has naturally led to higher spending on their health and well-being,” Mr. Saxena says.
Yet, pet insurance remains largely unfamiliar to the wider public. Unlike health or motor insurance, advertisements for pet insurance are rarely seen on hoardings, digital screens or mainstream media. Social media promotions, too, are often visible only to users whose online behaviour suggests an interest in pets.
Despite knowing that pet insurance existed, Ms. Aswathi was oblivious of its importance and the financial benefits it could offer.
Dr. N.K. Buddhan, a former veterinary doctor who now works as an insurance consultant for United India Insurance, says pet insurance is generally promoted through specialised channels.
“Pet insurance is promoted through dedicated channels like veterinary hospitals, kennel clubs and pet shows,” he says.
Dr. Buddhan has even encountered cases involving dogs valued at around ₹2 crore, whose owners insured them against untoward incidents during transportation and training.
Hospitals as a channel for awareness
Veterinary hospitals are increasingly becoming an important channel for spreading awareness about pet insurance. Dr. Soorej’s Cochin Pet Hospital is among those encouraging pet parents to consider insurance as the cost of pet ownership and medical treatment continues to rise. Many hospitals, including Cochin Pet Hospital, now discuss insurance options with their clients.
“A premium that starts with an annual premium of just ₹1700 saves a lot of money that the pet parents don’t realise they spend,” he said.
Your pet got a cover?
“Overall, the portfolio has recorded a CAGR of approximately 20%, reflecting the growing awareness among pet parents about the importance of protecting their pet’s health,” says Mr Saxena. “Pet insurance is a category that makes strong financial sense, and its growth prospects are promising.”
The growing adoption of pet insurance is also evident at veterinary hospitals. Dr. Soorej says the steady increase in customers opting for insurance at his hospital reflects pet parents’ growing willingness to invest in high-quality healthcare for their animals.
Dr Budhhan notes that the policy he endorses covers pets between six months and eight years of age against a wide range of diseases and accidents, as well as risks such as theft.
Insurers are also expanding the scope of coverage with new and unconventional features. For instance, ICICI Lombard has introduced ‘behavioural support’ for pets, covering interventions for abnormal stress and psychological adjustment issues, including severe anxiety, trauma and difficulties adapting to new circumstances.
“Reports show that Indian pet parents increasingly view pets as emotional companions, leading to higher spending on specialised care and lifestyle support. Behavioural issues often escalate into health problems, making early intervention crucial. By adding behaviour support, the service delivers holistic care that aligns with evolving pet parent expectations,” says Girish Sehgal, Chief of Health Underwriting & Claims, Customer Service & Operations at ICICI Lombard.
Is pet insurance practical?
A pioneering Malayalam sitcom once had a hilarious episode featuring the fictional ‘Thekkummoottil Insurance Corporation’, which, in an absurdly funny twist, offered insurance for “dogs also”. In the 2000s, the idea of insuring a dog was largely a punchline. Today, however, pet insurance is emerging as a serious and rapidly growing business, with insurers introducing increasingly specialised products for pet parents.
According to research by IMARC, India’s pet insurance market generated revenue of $331.1 million in 2025. The market is projected to show a CAGR of 12.6% between 2026 and 2034, reaching an estimated $993.4 million by 2034.
A pioneer in promoting pet insurance, like Dr. Buddhan, has more than just compelling stories about pet insurance to share; he also has plenty to say about how it can remain an inaccessible form of security for many pet parents.
From his experience, not many pet owners are keen on insuring their pets, despite insurance plans offered by several brands covering dogs and cats against a range of risks, from accidental poisoning to serious illnesses. One of the key reasons, he says, is the lack of feasibility of implementing insurance processes in veterinary hospitals.
Dr. R. Jayaprakash, founder of J.P. Pet Speciality Hospital, says the absence of proper documentation at many veterinary hospitals makes the process particularly difficult. “Most hospitals do not maintain a proper database, which makes it difficult to claim pet insurance,” he says.
He adds that many hospitals are reluctant to process cashless claims because reimbursements can take months or even years. “Many diagnoses can cost a hefty amount, but one will not get an insurance claim unless the pet is admitted to the hospital,” he says.
Such limitations leave pet owners with little incentive to purchase insurance, a situation that is equally discouraging for insurance agents looking to promote policies through veterinary hospitals, Dr. Jayaprakash adds.
“I have asked insurance agents to simplify the insurance criteria, which would encourage pet owners to buy policies,” he says.

briefs.headline: Output overdrive: 30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing
briefs.deck: According to a KPMG report, productivity is identified as the leading catalyst for growth within manufacturing. Firms that excel in boosting productivity tend to see notable increases in both profits and market valuation. For large manufacturers, meaningful productivity improvements require transformative approaches. Meanwhile, small factories are shown to have lower per-worker output. Leveraging…
briefs.bodyText:
India's manufacturing sector could get nearly 35 per cent of its future output simply by getting its workforce 30 per cent more productive.
The finding comes from KPMG's analysis of more than 130 large Indian manufacturing companies over 10 years. It found that companies which improved productivity faster than their peers also saw stronger growth in profits and market value.
Their net profits grew by around 10-11 per cent annually, compared with about 7 per cent for companies with average productivity.
The difference was even wider in market value. Companies leading in productivity recorded around 19 per cent CAGR in market capitalisation, against nearly 10 per cent for average-productivity organisations.
Overall, productivity-leading companies saw more than 50 per cent higher profitability growth and twice the market-cap expansion compared with their peers.
Small factories lag larger firms
The gains, however, are not spread evenly across the manufacturing sector.
More than 70 per cent of large manufacturing companies would need transformative measures to achieve the productivity growth rate required for India's manufacturing ambition, the report said.
There is also a wide gap between smaller and larger factories. Small and unorganised manufacturing facilities produce less than 20 per cent of the output per worker compared with large firms.
Even among companies within the manufacturing sector, productivity can vary sharply, with differences ranging between 300 per cent and 1,000 per cent.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
Six ways to drive manufacturing growth
KPMG identified six broad levers for manufacturing growth:
- Productivity
- Workforce shifts
- Global integration
- Investment in capacity
- Innovation and technology
- Consumption-led growth.
But productivity stands out because its benefits can continue over time.
“Productivity is Indian manufacturing's most powerful growth lever,” the report said, adding that productivity gains “embed permanently into the system, raising output, margins, and competitiveness year after year.”
“Unlike scale or demand-led levers, productivity improvements embed permanently into the system,” the report said.
The report said improving productivity would require companies to rethink how work is organised, how organisations are structured and how their workforce is deployed.
Digital and AI tools, performance management and changes in workplace culture would also be needed to support these changes, it said.

briefs.headline: India’s car buyers shift from petrol as CNG, hybrid, EVs cross 42% sales share: Report
briefs.deck: Cleaner fuels now lead Indian passenger vehicle sales, surpassing petrol for the first time. CNG's market share reached a record high of twenty-five percent in August. Electric vehicle sales saw a significant fifty-two percent jump year-on-year. Tata Motors regained its leading position in the electric vehicle market. Delhi recorded the highest electric car penetration, boosted by fleet…
briefs.bodyText:
India’s passenger vehicle market is reportedly seeing a notable shift in consumer preference away from petrol, with CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles together accounting for 42% of sales in August 2026.
For the first time, the combined share of these cleaner-fuel alternatives surpassed petrol, whose share fell to a record low of 41 per cent in August, compared with 46 per cent a year earlier, according to report by Equirus Securities, cited by ANI. CNG, meanwhile, rose to a record-high 25 per cent, up from 21% in August 2025.
The shift came as overall passenger vehicle retail sales grew 16 per cent year-on-year in August, helped by improved affordability following GST rate cuts.
Electric vehicles also continued to gain ground. EV sales jumped 52% year-on-year to 30,700 units during the month, taking their penetration to 7.7 per cent, compared with 5.9 per cent a year earlier. However, the figure was slightly lower than the 8.1 per cent penetration recorded in July 2026.
“Buyer hesitation around the E20 transition appears to have supported the shift towards CNG, hybrids and EVs,” Equirus Securities said in its report.
Among EV manufacturers, Tata Motors’ share recovered to around 43 per cent in August, its highest level since December 2025, compared with 42 per cent in July and 41 per cent a year earlier. The report attributed the recovery to Tata’s broad EV portfolio and the recent launch of the Tiago EV.
JSW MG Motor, meanwhile, saw its EV market share fall sharply to around 15 per cent in August from 28 per cent a year earlier amid intensifying competition. Mahindra & Mahindra’s share also slipped to around 21 per cent from 23 per cent in July. Maruti Suzuki, which has recently entered the EV segment, captured around 5 per cent of the electric car market.
Delhi emerged as the country’s leading market for electric cars in August, although fleet registrations boosted the headline figure. “Regionally, Delhi recorded the highest electric car penetration at ~19 per cent in Aug’26, although this was inflated by fleet registrations,” the report said.
Excluding VinFast-supplied taxi fleet registrations, the report estimated Delhi’s underlying EV penetration at around 12-14 per cent, still significantly above the national level of 7.7 per cent.

briefs.headline: Rs 41.69 lakh cash deposits, no ITR: He said wife, father paid expenses; ITAT rejects plea
briefs.deck: Reddy said he discovered the notice relating to the unexplained cash deposits only when he applied for a visa for foreign travel. He claimed that the Embassy informed him that an ITR was required for the visa application, which was when he came to know about the tax proceedings. The Income Tax Officer, however, did not accept this explanation.
briefs.bodyText:
When filing for a visa to fly abroad, an individual claimed he discovered he had a tax notice against his name that was due to cash deposits which the 
Income Tax Department
 saw as unexplained.
The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Bangalore has declined to condone the delay of nearly four years in the case concerning unexplained cash deposits. The taxpayer told the tribunal that he became aware of the tax notice only when he was seeking a visa to travel overseas.
Rs 41 lakh cash deposit but less than Rs 5 lakh income: What the case was about
The case involved Reddy, a resident of Indiranagar, Bengaluru, who maintained that his annual income was below Rs 5 lakh and that rent was his only source of income. According to Reddy, his wife and father took care of his expenses, which was why he neither filed income tax returns (ITRs) nor regularly checked his emails or the income tax e-filing portal, ET reported.
Reddy said he discovered the notice relating to the unexplained cash deposits only when he applied for a visa for foreign travel. He claimed that the Embassy informed him that an ITR was required for the visa application, which was when he came to know about the tax proceedings.
The Income Tax Officer, however, did not accept this explanation. The officer treated Rs 41.69 lakh as unexplained cash deposits under Section 69A, besides adding Rs 3.69 lakh as unexplained credit and Rs 1.5 lakh as business or professional income. 
Interest was also levied and penalty proceedings were initiated.
The Commissioner of Appeals (CIT A) upheld the additions as well as the penalties. Reddy then challenged the orders before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Bangalore.
The tribunal dismissed his appeal on August 17, 2026.
Why did he lose the case?
Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the ITAT Bangalore was dealing with three connected appeals in the matter. These related to the assessment of Reddy’s income and penalties imposed under Sections 270A and 271AAC of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
According to Surana, the assessment appeared to have been completed ex parte because Reddy failed to respond to notices issued by the Income Tax Department. He also did not contest the Assessing Officer’s orders before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) within the prescribed time.
By the time the matter reached the tribunal, there was a delay of approximately 1,480 days in filing the quantum appeal. The two penalty appeals were each filed after a delay of around 1,298 days.
Reddy attributed the prolonged delay to several factors. He said he had limited understanding of income-tax proceedings and was not in the habit of filing ITRs because his income was relatively low. He also said that he did not regularly monitor his emails or the income-tax portal and that the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic had further affected the situation.
According to Reddy, he became aware of the assessment and penalty orders only in March 2023, when he needed his income-tax returns for an overseas visa application. After learning about the proceedings, he approached a tax professional and subsequently filed the appeals.
The CIT(A)/NFAC, however, refused to condone the delay. It found that the explanations offered by Reddy were broad in nature and were not backed by documentary evidence.
The ITAT Bangalore concurred with this view. It pointed out that Reddy had filed income-tax returns in earlier years, making his claim that he was completely unaware of his income-tax compliance obligations difficult to accept.
The tribunal also took note of the fact that Reddy had sold a property for Rs 39 lakh in an earlier year without filing an ITR. It rejected his argument that earning less than Rs 5 lakh by itself meant that he was not required to file a return, since the basic exemption limit applicable at the time was lower.
Surana says: “Further, the ITAT Bangalore found that Reddy had not explained his prolonged inaction, particularly for the period extending beyond the pandemic.”
In reaching its conclusion, the ITAT Bangalore relied on the Supreme Court ruling in 2023 INSC 885, 
Sheo Raj Singh (Deceased) through L.Rs. and Ors. vs. Union of India (UOI)
, which dealt with the issue of condonation of delay.
The tribunal stressed that even a substantial delay can be condoned where the taxpayer provides a satisfactory and credible explanation. However, the power to condone such a delay cannot be exercised simply because the circumstances may invite sympathy.
It is for the taxpayer to establish that a genuine cause prevented the appeal from being filed within the prescribed period. In Reddy’s case, the ITAT Bangalore found that the reasons given amounted to excuses rather than a sufficiently supported explanation. It therefore upheld the decision not to condone the delay and dismissed all three appeals as time-barred.
An important aspect of the ruling, Surana points out, is that the ITAT Bangalore did not decide whether the additions made under Section 69A or the penalties imposed under Sections 270A and 271AAC were legally correct on their merits. Since the appeals were rejected at the threshold on the ground of limitation, the assessment and penalty orders were left intact and continued to have legal effect.
As a result, the tax, interest and penalties arising from those orders remain payable, to the extent that they have not already been paid, recovered or stayed.
Surana says Reddy could consider approaching the jurisdictional High Court against the ITAT Bangalore ruling under Section 260A, provided the matter involves a substantial question of law. This could include a legally sustainable challenge to the tribunal’s refusal to condone the delay.
Surana says: “However, the filing of a further appeal does not automatically suspend recovery. Unless a competent authority or court grants a stay, the Department may proceed to recover the outstanding demand. Thus, as matters presently stand, Reddy remains liable to discharge the tax, interest and penalties arising from the underlying orders.”

stories.headline: KCL: Imran sparkles as Titans emerge champions in a gripping finale
stories.bodyText:
Thrissur Titans overcame a stutter to beat a resilient Calicut Globstars by four wickets and win its maiden KCL title at the Sports Hub Greenfield Stadium in a final which started on Saturday and ended in the wee hours of Sunday.
Captain M.S. Akhil slammed Ibnul Afthaf over the deep square-leg fence to seal Titans’ triumph in the final over. Titans nearly messed up the chase and it needed a cameo from Akhil (19 n.o., 11b, 1x4, 1x6) to take them home.
After restricting Globstars to a below-par total of 167 for nine, Titans were cruising when Ahammed Imran (69, 49b, 7x4, 2x6) was going great guns. But Jose Perayil gave Globstars a big boost when he dismissed both Imran and Sanjeev Satheesan (29) in the 16th over.
T. Nikhil (14) perished to a catch in the deep and Mohammed Enaan (eight), too, fell when Titans were close to victory. However, Akhil kept his cool to secure the title for his side.
Imran underlined his growing stature as Kerala’s next big star by playing a well-paced knock until a rush of blood cost him his wicket.
Imran walked in after opener Vishnu Raj fell in the first over.
He began by uppercutting Akhin Sathar for a boundary and followed it up with a crisp cover drive off Ibnul.
He was the dominant partner in the 87-run third-wicket stand with Sanjeev who came in as concussion substitute for the injured Shoun Roger.
Imran reached his fifty with a reverse-scooped boundary off Jose. His dismissal against the run of play gave Globstars a sniff of a chance.
Earlier, opting to bat, Globstars were pegged back in the PowerPlay.
Akhil Scaria (45) and Aswin Anand (40) added a brisk 70 for the third wicket, taking chances against the spinners.
Biju Narayanan broke the threatening stand by forcing a poor shot from Scaria and Aswin followed him soon after, falling to leg-spinner Akhil. However, Globstars struggled to force the pace against some crafty bowling by Titans at the death.
Prized scalp
Left-arm medium-pacer Abdul Ramees bowled an excellent spell and took the big wicket of Salman Nizar.

stories.headline: Trinity Rodman's US Open moment reveals an old habit in sports broadcasting: introducing women by their relationships first
stories.deck: Trinity Rodman was introduced at the US Open as Ben Shelton’s girlfriend, frustrating fans who felt her Olympic and football achievements deserved greater recognition. Despite being an Olympic gold medallist, NWSL champion and highest-paid women’s footballer, Rodman was presented through her relationship with Shelton. The incident reignited debate over how female athletes are introduced and…
stories.bodyText:
Trinity Rodman was sitting in Ben Shelton's player box at the US Open on Tuesday when the cameras found her.
The ESPN commentary that followed introduced her as “Trinity Rodman, also known as Ben Shelton's girlfriend, and also known as a member of the US women's national team.” The on-screen graphic was similarly arranged: “Ben's girlfriend & USWNT player.”
Rodman is, of course, Shelton's girlfriend. The two tennis and football stars made their relationship public in March 2025, after Rodman slid into Shelton's DMs. Shelton, 23, is one of American tennis's leading players, a left-handed power hitter who reached a career-high world No.5 in late 2025 and has already won four ATP titles in 2026, including the National Bank Open two weeks before the US Open.
But Rodman has spent the better part of her career becoming recognisable without him.
The 24-year-old is an Olympic gold medallist, an NWSL champion and the highest-paid women's footballer in the world. She is also the daughter of NBA Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman, another fact that has often followed her into introductions of her own.
Soccer player Trinity Rodman celebrates after her boyfriend Ben Shelton, of the United States, won his match against Hubert Hurkacz, of Poland, during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Kirsty Wigglesworth)
The ESPN description prompted a familiar reaction from fans online, particularly because there was no shortage of things from Rodman's own career that could have been used instead.
“Geez… she is so much more than Ben's girlfriend,” one fan wrote.
Another put it more bluntly: “Trin is an Olympic gold medalist, NWSL player and then Ben's girlfriend. In that order.”
Rodman's career does not need Shelton's name attached to it
Rodman's football career began long before she became a fixture in Shelton's box.
The Washington Spirit selected her No.2 overall in the 2021 NWSL Draft when she was 18, making her the youngest player ever selected at the time. She won the league's Rookie of the Year award and helped Washington win the NWSL Championship in her first season.
Three years later, she produced one of the defining moments of her international career.
In the 2024 Paris Olympics final, Rodman scored in extra time against Japan as the United States won women's football gold for the first time since 2012. She now has 13 goals in 57 appearances for the USWNT.
At club level, her value has grown just as quickly. Rodman became the first player signed under the NWSL's High Impact Player rule and agreed a landmark deal with Washington worth more than $1 million per season through 2028, making her the highest-paid player in the league.
FILE - Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman in action during the second half of an NWSL soccer match against the Portland Thorns FC, Friday, March 13, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Terrance Williams,File)
There is also the question of her surname, which has brought its own assumptions.
Rodman has spoken openly about her complicated relationship with her father and rejected the idea that the name defines her.
“He’s not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else,” she said on 
Call Her Daddy
.
“I love to have my last name and when I say Rodman, it’s not my dad’s name, it’s my name.”
She has been less defensive about being known as Shelton's partner. In fact, Rodman has said she actually likes the term 
WAG
, even while acknowledging why some people dislike it.
“For me, I think I like the term personally because, like I said before, I feel like 24/7 I'm on in front of cameras, and so I think I use the term WAG for me to simplify what I'm doing,” she said on 
Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce
 in August.
“For me, saying WAG, it's me being like, ‘I'm Ben's girlfriend.’ But I can understand why it's so hated.”
She described being able to share that experience with Shelton as “the best feeling in the world”, pointing to the fact that both are constantly training, competing and exhausting themselves doing the sports they love.
That distinction matters. Rodman choosing to embrace the label is not the same thing as it being the most useful way to introduce her.
This has happened before
The US Open moment was not the first time Rodman's identity has been filtered through the people around her.
At Wimbledon in 2025, she was introduced during one of Shelton's matches as “Tiffany” and had her father mentioned in the same breath.
This time, the mistake was different. Her name was right, her relationship was real and her football career was acknowledged. Yet the order still said something: Ben's girlfriend first, USWNT player second.
Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman shoots as Seattle Reign FC midfielder Samantha Meza, right, looks on during the first half of an NWSL soccer match, Sunday, May 10, 2026, in Seattle. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson)
There was plenty of room for a different introduction.
Rodman was not simply another celebrity sitting in a tennis player's box. She was an Olympic champion watching another elite American athlete compete at one of the biggest sporting events in the world.
She can be Ben Shelton's girlfriend. She can be Dennis Rodman's daughter. She can even happily call herself a WAG.
None of those things requires her own achievements to come second.
At 24, Trinity Rodman has already built a career substantial enough to stand on its own. At the US Open, she happened to be there to support someone else.
For once, she deserved the spotlight without needing to be introduced through him.

stories.headline: Shafali scripts history, becomes fastest and youngest to reach 3,000 T20I runs
stories.deck: At just twenty-two years and 220 days old, Shafali Verma made history by becoming the youngest player ever to score 3,000 runs in T20 internationals. She also claimed the title for the fastest to reach this milestone in terms of balls faced. In a decisive match, India easily chased down Pakistan's meager total of fifty-six, securing a resounding seven-wicket victory.
stories.bodyText:
Shafali Varma created history during India’s Women’s Asia Cup 2026 clash against Pakistan in Dubai on Saturday, becoming the youngest player to score 3,000 runs in women’s T20Is. The India opener reached the landmark at the age of 22 years and 220 days, surpassing Ireland’s Gaby Lewis, who previously held the record at 24 years and 347 days.
Shafali also became the fastest batter to reach 3,000 runs in women’s T20Is in terms of balls faced, achieving the feat in just 2,182 deliveries. She is the 16th player overall to reach 3,000 runs in women’s T20Is and the third Indian after 
Smriti Mandhana
 and 
Harmanpreet Kaur
.
Youngest to 3000 runs in Women’s T20Is
- 22y 220d - Shafali Verma (IND-W)
- 24y 347d - Gaby Lewis (IRE-W)
- 27y 139d - Esha Oza (UAE-W)
- 27y 171d - Smriti Mandhana (IND-W)
- 27y 347d - Hayley Matthews (WI-W)
A brief but explosive outing
Shafali reached the landmark in typically aggressive fashion. She opened the innings with a six off Sadia Iqbal before taking a single from the next ball to bring up her 3,000 T20I runs. She then smashed Fatima Sana for a powerful four before departing for 12 off six balls, including one four and one six.
Fatima dismissed her caught and bowled in the second over, with Shafali getting a leading edge that ballooned back to the Pakistan captain.
India chase down 56 with ease
Shafali’s early dismissal did little to trouble India, who were chasing just 56 after Pakistan were bowled out for their lowest-ever T20I total. Pakistan’s batting collapsed against India’s spin attack, with Shree Charani and Prema Rawat taking three wickets each, while Deepti Sharma claimed two.
India comfortably completed the chase, reaching 57/3 in 8.4 overs to register a dominant seven-wicket victory and finish at the top of Group A. Harmanpreet Kaur remained unbeaten on 18 and finished the match in style with a six.

briefs.headline: When young minds learn from the masters
briefs.bodyText:
The last time Magnus Carlsen gave a display of simultaneous chess in India, he was in for a surprise. And he spoke about it just before he took on 25 young players a few hours before the fourth edition of the Global Chess League got underway here on Saturday.
Carlsen had come to Chennai in 2013 for a reconnaissance ahead of his first World title match, against Viswanathan Anand. He agreed to play with 20 youngsters.
“I was told the players were some school champions, and I wasn’t aware that I was going to take on some really strong players,” the World No. 1 recalled. “I had jet-lag, and my opponents included Pragg (R. Praggnanandhaa), Vaishali and Aravindh Chithambaram. I don’t even remember how many games I lost.”
He actually lost four, one of which was against Vaishali. And he drew six; Praggnananandhaa and Aravindh were among the players that held him.
The organisers of the simultaneous event, Yippee, principal sponsor of Carlsen’s GCL franchise, Alpine APL Pipers, sprang no such surprise. There was only one strong player, Pratitee Bordoloi, who recently won the Asian junior girls’ championship. And she, in fact, came in as a last-minute replacement for one of the players.
Indian Grandmasters Koneru Humpy and Vidit Gujrathi also took on the youngsters alongside Carlsen. Another Grandmaster, Pravin Thipsay, the coach of Alpine Pipers, was also there, to explain the rules to the kids.
Vidit spoke of his own experience of playing simultaneous chess against a Grandmaster, from the other side of the board, as a little boy. Later, on Thipsay revealed he was that Grandmaster.
“I had played against kids at Nasik and I remember my six-year-old opponent,” said Thipsay. “I found him pretty good in positional play even at that age. And I told his father that the boy showed a lot of promise.”

briefs.headline: Women’s Asia Cup T20: Spinners headline India’s crushing 7-wicket win vs Pakistan

briefs.bodyText:
Left-arm spinner Shree Charani was the star performer, returning brilliant figures of 3 for 7, with able support from young leg-spinner Prema Rawat, as India dismantled Pakistan for a paltry 55 in 18.1 overs without breaking much sweat in an inconsequential Group A league game of the Women's Asia Cup here on Saturday (September 5, 2026).
This was Pakistan's lowest score in history of T20 Internationals.
Opting to bat, Pakistan did start confidently, reaching 27 for no loss in little over four overs with openers Muneeba Ali (13) and Shawaal Zulfiqar (14) facing the seamers with ease, but none of the other batters was able to reach double figures in an embarrassing display of ineptitude.
The two wrist spinners Shafali Verma (1/10 in 3 overs) and Prema (3/9 in 4 overs) didn't try to turn and kept attacking the stumps with relentless accuracy. By the time, Deepti Sharma (2/5 in 3.1 overs) came into bowl, Pakistan women had already thrown in the towel. In 18.1 overs, Indian bowlers delivered an astounding 78 dot balls.
Once, Harmanpreet Kaur, captaining the country for the 150th time in T2Ois, gauged that the pitch is offering turn, she introduced the spinners right away and got due dividends. Suddenly Pakistan lost six wickets for addition of 9 runs to totter at 36 for 6 after end of 10 overs.

briefs.headline: India crush Pakistan by 7 wickets after spin attack bundles them out for 55
briefs.deck: In a stunning performance, India triumphed over Pakistan by seven wickets during their Group A encounter. Pakistan struggled significantly, managing a mere 55 runs, marking their lowest T20I score. India's spinners dominated, with Shree Charani leading the charge by taking three wickets. Shafali Verma made history by surpassing 3,000 T20I runs. With this victory, India completed the group stage…
briefs.bodyText:
India produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Pakistan by seven wickets in their Group A clash of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Saturday.
After Pakistan opted to bat first, India’s spinners ran riot, bowling them out for just 55 in 18.1 overs, their lowest-ever total in T20Is. India then chased down the modest target in only 8.4 overs, reaching 57/3 with 68 balls to spare.
The victory saw India finish the group stage at the top of Group A, having already sealed their semi-final spot with wins over Thailand and Hong Kong.
Pakistan collapse under India’s spin attack
Pakistan never found their footing after being asked to bat. Shawaal Zulfiqar top-scored with 14, while Muneeba Ali made 13, but no other batter managed to offer sustained resistance. India’s spin attack was relentless. Shree Charani and Prema Rawat claimed three wickets apiece, while Deepti Sharma picked up two. Shafali Verma also chipped in with a wicket as India’s spinners accounted for all 10 Pakistan wickets.
Charani returned excellent figures of 3/7 from four overs, while Rawat finished with 3/9. 
Deepti was equally economical, conceding just five runs for her two wickets. Pakistan’s collapse was particularly dramatic after they lost six wickets for just 15 runs, leaving them struggling at the bottom of the innings. Their 55 all out marked their lowest total in T20I cricket.
Shafali gives India flying start
India’s chase began aggressively, with Shafali Verma smashing 12 off just six balls, including a six. She also crossed the landmark of 3,000 T20I runs during her brief stay at the crease.
Fatima Sana provided Pakistan with their only real resistance, dismissing Shafali, Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana to finish with impressive figures of 3/17. Despite those breakthroughs, the target was far too small to give Pakistan any genuine hope.
Captain 
Harmanpreet Kaur
 held the chase together and finished unbeaten on 18 off 18 balls. She completed the victory in style, hitting a six as India reached 57/3 in 8.4 overs. The result extended India’s overall T20I head-to-head advantage over Pakistan to 15-3 and their Women’s Asia Cup record to 7-1.
More importantly, India finished the group stage in pole position and head into the semi-finals without any loss.

briefs.headline: India’s spin chokehold leaves Pak in tatters: 55 all out is their lowest-ever total
briefs.deck: Pakistan suffered their lowest T20I score ever, bowled out for just 55 runs. India's bowlers, led by Charani and Rawat, triggered a dramatic batting collapse. Pakistan lost six wickets for only eight runs after a promising start. This historic low occurred during Pakistan's 200th T20 International match. India continued their strong record against Pakistan.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Pakistan endured a dramatic batting collapse against India in their Women’s Asia Cup 2026 clash in Dubai on Saturday, crashing to their lowest-ever total in T20I cricket after being bowled out for just 55.
After opting to bat first, Pakistan appeared to have an opportunity to put scoreboard pressure on India. Instead, their innings unravelled spectacularly as India’s bowlers turned the screw, with Pakistan losing six wickets for just eight runs after initially reaching 27 without loss.
The 55 all out is now Pakistan’s lowest total in Women’s T20Is, surpassing their previous low of 56 against New Zealand in Dubai in 2024. It also becomes the fifth-lowest total conceded by India in a Women’s T20I.
Only Pakistan’s two openers managed to cross double figures, with Muneeba Ali scoring 13 off 15 balls and Shawaal Zulfiqar making 14 from 14.
Charani, Rawat trigger spectacular collapse
The slide began after Muneeba survived a couple of early scares before Shafali Verma eventually cleaned her up. Sree Charani then struck twice in the final over of the powerplay, turning Pakistan’s promising start into a full-blown collapse.
Pakistan went from 27/0 to 35/6, with India’s spinners repeatedly breaching a batting line-up that struggled to cope with the pressure.
Charani finished with outstanding figures of 3/7, while Prema Rawat also claimed three wickets for just nine runs. Deepti Sharma chipped in with 2/5 and Shafali Verma took one wicket.
The Indian attack's ruthlessness was reflected in Pakistan's inability to build even a single substantial partnership after the opening stand. With wickets tumbling at regular intervals, the innings was wrapped up for 55 in 18.1 overs.
Charani credited a simple approach for her success.
"Just (trying) to bowl to my strength, and coaches are telling all bowlers, spinners especially, to bowl to strength and give more revs on the ball. [What deliveries are you working on?] Trying to get more consistency on my arm ball and be more accurate on the yorkers," she said at the break.
The performance underlined why India had entered the contest with such confidence in their bowling attack. India had already secured a place in the semi-finals after winning their opening two matches against Thailand and Hong Kong, while Pakistan came into the game having beaten Thailand.
Pakistan’s unwanted record in 200th T20I
The collapse came on a significant occasion for Pakistan, who were playing their 200th T20I. Instead of celebrating the landmark with a competitive total, they ended the innings with a record they would rather forget.
Pakistan’s previous lowest all-out total in the format was 56 against New Zealand in Dubai in 2024. Their other lowest totals included 60 against England in Taunton in 2009, 63 against India in Guangzhou in 2012 and 65 against the West Indies in St Andrew’s in 2011.
For India, meanwhile, the 55 all out added another dominant chapter to their recent record against Pakistan. India had won nine of their previous 10 T20I meetings, with their only defeat in that stretch coming in the 2022 Asia Cup.
The contest also marked Harmanpreet Kaur’s record 150th match as a T20I captain, making her the first cricketer, male or female, to reach the landmark.

briefs.headline: Duleep Trophy: Proven performers take centre stage in final showdown
briefs.deck: The presence of Padikkal and Siraj gives South the edge over East; however, Sooryavanshi could be the X-factor for Kishan’s men; Shreyas and Shami set for their 100th First Class game
briefs.bodyText:
The Indian cricketing calendar is jam-packed with international matches, the IPL and other State-run T20 leagues in addition to multi-format domestic competitions.
Nestled in this congested schedule, tournaments like the Duleep Trophy, once a marquee event in which the top players took part, are fighting for relevance.
Still, the powers that be have tried to keep the legacy events alive through numerous tweaks. Back in the zonal avatar since last year, this prestigious tournament is now the curtain-raiser for the domestic season, the summit clash of which will see South Zone take on East Zone here at the MAC Stadium from Sunday.
The next five days offer proven performers from last year and some of India’s top stars a chance to show their wares and fine-tune skills.
The arrival of Devdutt Padikkal and Mohammed Siraj has bolstered the Tilak Varma-led South.
Padikkal, who recently scored centuries in both Tests against Sri Lanka, in which he was also the Player-of-the-Series, will look to continue his purple patch.
In contrast, Siraj looked off colour against the Islanders and needs to use this opportunity to find his rhythm again.
The red-soil pitch at the Chepauk should offer some assistance to the quick on the first few days, and Siraj needs to make it count.
For Shreyas Gopal — who played a crucial role with the bat (87) in South’s victory over North Zone in the semifinals — it will be a special occasion as he will feature in his 100th First Class appearance.
Joining him in the landmark will be Mohammed Shami, whom East will depend on to reclaim the Duleep Trophy it last won at this venue in 2012. The pacer bagged five wickets in the semifinals against Central Zone and would want to continue his fine show as he keeps banging the door for a return to the national side.
Though Ishan Kishan’s men might look like the underdog on paper, the presence of teen sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi gives the outfit an X-factor. A Sooryavanshi special in a big game in the longest format could be the perfect appetiser for the domestic season.

briefs.headline: ‘Remarkable’: Ganguly’s special message for Shami ahead of 100th first-class game
briefs.deck: Mohammed Shami will play his 100th first-class match in the Duleep Trophy final. Sourav Ganguly congratulated Shami on this significant career milestone. Ganguly highlighted the difficulty for subcontinent fast bowlers to sustain careers. Shami is currently aiming for an international recall after a strong domestic showing. His captain Ishan Kishan praised Shami's hunger and determination on the…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Mohammed Shami
 is set to enter an elite club on Sunday when he makes his 100th first-class appearance in the Duleep Trophy final, and former India captain Sourav Ganguly believes the milestone is a fitting reward for the veteran pacer’s remarkable longevity and contribution to 
Indian cricket
.
Shami will turn out for East Zone against South Zone at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, with the occasion marking another significant chapter in a first-class career that has already produced 382 wickets from 99 matches. His best innings figures are 8/90.
Ganguly, who played alongside Shami during the early stages of the pacer’s career, congratulated him on the landmark and highlighted the difficulty of sustaining a career as a fast bowler in the subcontinent.
"Dear Shami, congratulations on achieving this amazing feat - 100 first-class matches. As a fast bowler in the subcontinent, it's a remarkable achievement. I've seen you grow; I've played with you. It was the early stages of your career and the end of my international career. I always knew there was talent, but I'm extremely happy that you've used that talent to go this distance," Ganguly said in a video posted by CAB on Facebook.
Ganguly also backed Shami to cap the milestone occasion with a Duleep Trophy title.
"And I enjoy the games. You're playing the Duleep Trophy final - it will be an icing on the cake if you win it. Your performances over the years have been fantastic, especially in Test cricket. You know, when fast bowlers shy away from playing Test cricket, you have a day-in, day-out run-in for India. Heartiest congratulations once again from my side and everyone at the Cricket Association of Bengal and the state of West Bengal. You know, it's a fabulous achievement. Enjoy the game and hope to see you soon," he added.
Shami’s milestone comes amid India comeback bid
The landmark comes at a particularly interesting stage of Shami’s career. The 36-year-old remains outside India’s current setup but has continued to play domestic cricket as he looks to maintain his fitness and put himself in contention for another international recall. He last played for India in the Champions Trophy final in March 2025.
Shami has made a strong impact in the Duleep Trophy. After going wicketless in East Zone’s opening match, he bounced back against defending champions Central Zone in the semi-final, taking five wickets across two innings as East secured a four-wicket victory and reached the final.
‘Age is just a number’, says Kishan
East Zone captain Ishan Kishan has been equally impressed by Shami’s determination and believes age should not stand in the way of the veteran’s ambitions.
“I think he is just one of the best. He has been a legend of this game. He has been doing so well since he started playing for Bengal. He has been picking wickets, giving all his energy and he has done so well for the Indian cricket team also,” Kishan said at the pre-match press conference.
“I feel age is just a number. If he is working hard it doesn't matter. I see that hunger in Shami bhai because who better than me to judge about hunger right now,” Kishan said, referring to his own period away from the Indian team.
That hunger was visible during the semi-final, when Shami asked for additional overs in his pursuit of wickets.
“Looking at his efforts as a captain, I felt very nice, because Shami bhai came in, asking me for those extra overs to get the wickets. This is something which always gives confidence to skippers. When you have bowlers who are willing to get you wickets, it's always good to have him in the team,” Kishan said.
Shami even contributed with the bat, hitting two boundaries and prompting a light-hearted verdict from his captain.
“He also finished with two boundaries, so he is an all-rounder I feel nowadays. So I am very happy to have him in my team,” he added.

briefs.headline: ‘This isn’t politics’: Brian Lara backs Imran Khan, calls for dignity and proper care
briefs.deck: Brian Lara and Pat Cummins join former captains supporting Imran Khan's treatment. They are calling for independent medical assessments and humane care. Concerns focus on Khan's reported vision problems while in custody. Khan denies corruption charges, which supporters claim are politically motivated. This appeal highlights basic humanity for a respected cricket legend.
briefs.bodyText:
Former West Indies captain Brian Lara has become the latest prominent cricket figure to voice support for imprisoned former Pakistan captain 
Imran Khan
, calling for proper medical care and humane treatment for the 1992 World Cup-winning skipper.
Lara took to Instagram to express his concern over Khan’s situation, saying he was struggling to understand how a sporting icon who once inspired an entire country could now find himself in circumstances where, in Lara’s view, he was not receiving the compassion and dignity he deserved.
"Imran Khan and I only crossed paths on the field a handful of times, but the respect I have for him was instant and lasting," Lara wrote in his Instagram post.
"I am struggling to understand how someone who was once a beacon of hope, pride and inspiration for his country, at the height of his sporting career, could now find himself in a situation where he is not being cared for and treated with the compassion and dignity he deserves.
"I stand with my fellow former captains in asking that he receive proper, independent medical care and the dignity every human being deserves. This isn't politics. 
It's basic humanity for a legend of our game," he added.
Lara joins growing chorus of cricket greats
Lara’s intervention comes amid growing concern among former and current international cricketers over Khan’s health and treatment in custody.
A group of former international captains, led by former Australia skipper Greg Chappell, has repeatedly called for Khan to receive an independent medical assessment, continued family access and any treatment recommended by doctors. The latest appeal was signed by 21 former captains, including Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Allan Border, Michael Atherton, Steve Waugh, Adam Gilchrist and Nasser Hussain.
The signatories described themselves as former colleagues and rivals whose bond was forged on the cricket field and urged authorities to ensure that a court-directed medical process was properly completed.
Their concerns have centred particularly on reports of significant vision problems affecting Khan’s right eye. The 73-year-old has been in custody since 2023 after being convicted in corruption cases that he has denied, while his supporters have described the cases as politically motivated.
Cummins also backs appeal
Earlier, Australia captain Pat Cummins has also publicly backed the campaign, becoming one of the most prominent active international cricketers to speak out on Khan’s treatment.
“Adding my support here to GC (Greg Chappell) and the other former international captains. I hope the court ordered medical assessment be allowed to run its course, and that family visits continue.
“I hope Imran Khan is treated with the dignity anyone deserves,” Cummins posted on X.
The campaign has called for three key measures: a comprehensive health evaluation by a Supreme Court-directed medical board that includes Khan’s personal physicians, uninterrupted weekly family visits, and immediate implementation of any recommended medical treatment.
Former Pakistan cricketers, including Moin Khan, have also raised their voices over the issue, with Moin recently urging other cricketers to speak up for the former captain’s wellbeing.

briefs.headline: Duleep Trophy Final | Will relentless Shami get another go at the international level?
briefs.deck: At a time when Jasprit Bumrah is battling injuries and Mohammed Siraj is not looking at his sharpest, another good run in domestic cricket could get Shami back in the reckoning
briefs.bodyText:
When Mohammed Shami walks onto the MAC Stadium turf on Sunday for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy final against South Zone, it will be a momentous occasion for the 36-year-old, who will be featuring in his 100th First Class match.
As he aims to return to the national team, Shami has been putting in the hard yards in domestic cricket. Last year, the pacer took 37 wickets in the Ranji Trophy from seven matches as Bengal narrowly missed out on making the summit clash.
This season, in two Duleep outings so far, the veteran speedster has bowled with pace and verve, prompting East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan to praise him lavishly.
“He has been picking up wickets, giving all his energy. He is coming in and asking me for those extra overs to get the wickets.
“It is hard when you are not regularly playing for the Indian team and to have that kind of motivation for domestic games. But I see that hunger in him.
“You can see when he is trying to help me — he comes and gives options about what can be done,” Kishan added.
At a time when Jasprit Bumrah is battling injuries and Mohammed Siraj is not looking at his sharpest, another good run in domestic cricket could get Shami back in the reckoning.
India’s next Test tour is to New Zealand, where conditions will be seamer-friendly. Shami can also be a great asset in the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, a tournament where he boasts of a stellar record — 55 wickets at a world-leading average of 13.52.
In the last Duleep game against Central Zone in Bengaluru, the way Shami set up Yash Rathod — testing the batter outside the off-stump, softening him up with a few bouncers before nipping one away to get him caught behind — showed a bowler still at the top of his game.
During that fixture, National selector Pragyan Ojha had a long discussion with the pacer from Amroha. Opening of a fresh chapter in Shami’s international career? Time will tell.
